description: We're 3andna 7al  on Lunar Landing Site Navigator: compare south-pole landing sites and dates with real Sun/Earth-above-horizon views for power and comm windows not a dead demo dashboard. In-house: backend, UI/UX, AI, security, full-stack; Space Apps 2022 satellites web; this round Horizons, LOLA, Moon Trek-style layers. Want lunar/geospatial, horizon windows, terrain + illumination viz, science storytelling, pitch help. We scope one tool, ship in 48h; build-first welcome.
summary:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator helps planners compare lunar south-pole sites and dates for when the centres of the Sun and Earth clear a flat 0° local horizon—centre-ray clearance from saved NASA/JPL Horizons data, not disc visibility, power, or a ground-station link.

We built an offline navigator that loads two sites on one shared UTC playhead, classifies each sample as Clear, Blocked, or Unknown for Sun-centre, Earth-centre, and Both-centres lanes, and exports the same engine result the timeline and inspector show. Terrain stays Unknown until a full skyline review; the demo uses the labeled 0° baseline so claims stay honest.

In the 48-hour practice replay, Site04 has 48 h of Sun-centre clearance and Malapert has none; both have 0 h of simultaneous Sun- and Earth-centre clearance. Longer January packs support the same centre-ray story. Replay works without a CDN so judges can verify offline.

Why it matters: south-pole planning needs transparent, timestamped site-to-site comparison against NASA ephemeris—not opaque averages—so educators and planners can see when illumination and Earth geometry look favorable together, and when they do not.
details:
**What it does / how it works**

Lunar Landing Site Navigator compares two lunar south-pole landing sites on one shared UTC timeline. For every saved time step it classifies whether the centre of the Sun and the centre of Earth are above a flat 0° local horizon (centre-ray clearance from NASA/JPL Horizons Quantity 4, apparent airless angles). Three lanes—Sun-centre, Earth-centre, and Both-centres—roll up into interval totals and an interactive timeline. Users can trace any headline number back to the exact Horizons row, open overlapping clear windows, and export the same JSON the engine used. Terrain skyline mode is selectable but remains Unknown until a full science review; the demo’s accepted claim is the labeled geometric 0° baseline.

**Benefits**

Planners and educators get a pairwise, timestamped story instead of a single-site table or an opaque average. The Both-centres lane shows when Sun and Earth geometry align for direct-Earth thinking—not a radio link or power budget. Offline replay (no CDN) lets reviewers verify classifications without calling JPL live. Explicit Unknown states for missing ephemeris or unreviewed terrain avoid silent wrong answers.

**Intended impact**

Support informed conversation about south-pole site and date tradeoffs: when one candidate gains Sun-centre hours, when Earth-centre stays blocked, and when simultaneous clearance is zero even if one body looks favorable. The tool is educational and planning-oriented, not an operations replacement for Horizons, STK, or mission comms analysis.

**Tools and stack**

Python engine (classification, streaming, comparison) with pytest coverage; saved Horizons CSV/JSON under `data/horizons/`; optional LOLA DEM assets for display-only skyline plots; vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript UI with vendored fonts and sanitised docs viewer; local HTTP serve on port 8766; release manifest with SHA listings; browser and notebook traces for independent checks. Development used Cursor-assisted implementation and review; centre-ray states always come from saved NASA data.

**Creativity**

We paired two real practice sites (Site04 and Malapert) on one playhead, made limitations visible in-app (banners, exports, judge Q&A), and built a “Why this result?” path from totals to raw rows. Minimum-duration window filtering answers planning-style questions (“4 h Sun-centre clear?”) without changing the engine. We ship both witnessed JSON replays and a live-streaming candidate from the same rules.

**Factors considered**

Centre-ray only—no disc visibility, received power, or ground-station contact claims. Malapert’s practice observer height and open Appendix B digest mismatch are documented. Lead approved the January Horizons packs for a 0° submission claim while terrain stays gated. We prioritized reproducibility, honest labeling, and Wi-Fi-off demo integrity over showing unreviewed terrain totals.
